Codex review: needs changes before merge. ## What this changes Routes explicitly conversation-targeted scheduled turns through ordinary session admission, execution, delivery, and settlement. **Example:** A scheduled report targets session:agent:main:project:inbox while another turn is active. - **Before:** Cron uses its separate execution path after waiting for the conversation. - **After:** The report joins the conversation’s ordinary queue, and Cron waits for terminal settlement. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | Useful ownership consolidation with meaningful runtime and authority evidence, but the remaining premature-completion regression blocks merge. | | **Proof confidence** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | Sufficient (terminal): For this maintainer-authored PR, the supplied isolated Gateway continuation run and production-owner controls cover allowed execution, queued revocation, forbidden workspace access, and revocation during publication; the latest route regression rejects the stale destination before the transport adapter while controls still send. | | **Patch quality** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | 1 actionable review finding remain. | ## Product **Kind:** Refactor · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Scheduled conversation work has a separate execution owner, making conversation queueing, authority, workspace custody, and completion harder to keep consistent. **Reason:** The maintainer-authored direction consolidates existing responsibility, preserves later migration boundaries, and explicitly approves the additive Claw review variants. ## Regression provenance Possible regression — suspected (reviewed change). No predecessor PR is attributed. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Needs changes before merge - 2 items remain** Keep this maintainer-authored PR open: the session-admission cutover is useful, but the previously reported scheduled-send finality regression remains unfixed. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `78c8fa1884a7b5fc434f0b2b3e286d77b17bfb0a` ## Before merge - [ ] **Preserve Cron’s nonfinal default for scheduled message sends (P1)** - This previously reported finding remains unfixed. For a session-targeted announce job that sends to its configured destination with final omitted and then updates a ledger, both adapters consume this builder without messageToolFinalByDefault. resolveMessageToolSourceReplyFinal consequently defaults to true, and the embedded terminal hook can complete the turn immediately after the send, skipping the ledger update. Forward scheduledAutomation.sourceDelivery.messageTool.finalByDefault here and cover continued execution after the send, preserving the contract from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176141. - [ ] **Explain or restore the original intent of Scheduled message-send finality** - 075b46634555fa317782a0f4d88e158faa935e42: A configured Cron destination must not end the job when final is omitted, because post-send steps still need to run. ## Findings - [P1] Preserve Cron’s nonfinal default for scheduled message sends — `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-run-params.ts:173-177` ### Provenance - `Scheduled message-send finality` changes intended behavior without addressing why it exists (075b46634555fa317782a0f4d88e158faa935e42: A configured Cron destination must not end the job when final is omitted, because post-send steps still need to run.) ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: The supplied proof does not exercise a session-targeted same-destination send with final omitted followed by a real ledger write.
Agent review details ### How this fits together Cron supplies scheduled work and captured authority to the session controller; ordinary reply execution produces tool effects, delivery evidence, and a terminal result for Cron history. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Cron occurrence] --> B[Session event admission] B --> C[Conversation controller] C --> D[Reply execution] D --> E[Embedded or CLI runtime] E --> F[Tools and delivery] F --> G[Terminal settlement] G --> A ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Forward Cron’s existing message-tool finality default through the shared candidate builder and preserve send-then-continue behavior through ordinary session execution. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Source establishes the failing path: scheduled candidates omit the finality override, the resolver defaults omitted final to true, and a confirmed same-target send terminates embedded execution; no target code was run during this review. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Reusing ordinary session admission is the right ownership direction, and the smallest remaining repair is one shared parameter projection rather than another execution or delivery owner. Full review comments: - [P1] Preserve Cron’s nonfinal default for scheduled message sends — `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-run-params.ts:173-177` This previously reported finding remains unfixed. For a session-targeted announce job that sends to its configured destination with final omitted and then updates a ledger, both adapters consume this builder without messageToolFinalByDefault. resolveMessageToolSourceReplyFinal consequently defaults to true, and the embedded terminal hook can complete the turn immediately after the send, skipping the ledger update.
